In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and characterization of novel Ir(III) complexes containing N(6)-aminoacid-adenines.
the synthesis and characterization of new NAMI-A analogs with adenine modified with aminoacids.
the synthesis, structural characterization, biological activity and molecular modeling of three novel Ir(III) complexes with modified adenine derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all complexes are active against all three cell lines, with a higher activity for the N6-modified adenine with longer aminoacid chains.
the NAMI-A analogues (1-3), although they do not show any cytotoxic effect, have the ability to interact with the double stranded DNA.
the N(6)-modified adenine ligands are not able to improve the anticancer activity and DNA cleavage ability of the NAMI-A derivatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three complexes show a good antitumor activity against the three cell lines.
these compounds have a potential for use as antitumor agents, but further studies are required to understand the mechanisms of their action.
the complexes (1-2) have a good ability to cleave double stranded plasmid DNA, while (3) has a lower activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aminoacid chain has a significant influence on the interaction between Ir(III)-NAMI-A and DNA.
the presence of a lp-π interaction between the metal and the adenine ring has a significant effect on the cytotoxicity and the DNA binding properties.
the presence of the N3H+ moiety and the lp-π interaction are important for DNA cleavage activity.
